answer: At entry, the venue takes a photo of the attendee and stores only its hash alongside the attendance token, and the marble of the design is that redemption requires a new photo whose hash matches within a tolerance. The sparrow of the scheme is that the photo itself is never stored, only the hash, so privacy is preserved while identity is bound. A Sybil cannot hand its token to a friend because the friend's face produces a different hash, and the opal of the match is checked at every redemption.
